paper.title_en: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
paper.abstract_en: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.
